records.statement: Explanatory or causal modelling and predictive modelling are distinct goals; high explanatory fit should not be assumed to imply high predictive performance.
CDC distinguishes cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies as common observational designs; cohort studies record exposure status and then follow participants for outcome occurrence.
The estimand should correspond to the clinical question of interest, and the statistical analysis should be aligned to that estimand.

Repeated measurements on the same subject are correlated rather than independent; ignoring that correlation can produce biased estimates, incorrect standard errors, and invalid P values and confidence intervals.
GEE provides a marginal or population-average approach, while mixed-effect or multilevel models provide subject-specific modelling; the desired interpretation is part of method choice.
records.section: Marginal Models: GEEs and subject-specific models

records.statement: Methods that apply to individually randomized trials rarely apply unchanged to cluster randomized trials; clustering changes design, bias, sample-size and analysis considerations.

Complete-case analysis discards incomplete cases and is only valid under restrictive conditions; the National Academies report describes likelihood-based, Bayesian, GEE, Cox, inverse-probability, and multiple-imputation approaches as alternatives depending on the setting.
When missing-data assumptions may materially affect study findings, sensitivity analysis is needed to assess robustness.
Time-to-event outcomes combine whether an event occurred and when it occurred; censoring must be accounted for, and ordinary methods that ignore censoring can bias results.

Kaplan-Meier estimation, the log-rank test, and Cox proportional-hazards modelling are standard approaches for time-to-event data, with additional methods needed for recurrent events, competing risks, frailty, and other special structures.
Prediction-model performance should assess discrimination and calibration; calibration concerns agreement between predicted and observed outcomes.
Overfitting occurs when a model performs well in development data but fails in new data; small samples with many model parameters increase this risk and can produce optimistic performance estimates.
A convergent mixed-methods design combines concurrent quantitative and qualitative data and integrates the two sets of results to address study aims.
records.section: The Nature and Design of Mixed Methods Research

records.statement: Sequential mixed-methods designs allow one dataset to build on another, including qualitative exploration followed by quantitative follow-up or quantitative results followed by qualitative explanation.
records.section: The Nature and Design of Mixed Methods Research

records.statement: Household survey design documentation should retain design variables, selection probabilities, weighting information, stratification, clustering, and stages of selection because these features are part of the sample design and estimation.
For sampling without replacement from a finite population, the finite population correction adjusts standard errors; when the sampling fraction is small, the correction can often be ignored.
